content.text: The text begins as an extensive medical index covering diseases, symptoms, anatomy, treatments, and page references, ending Volume II. It then shifts to Thomas Paine’s biography: his *Age of Reason* provoked numerous replies, notably Bishop Watson’s concessions and Erskine’s prosecution of publisher Thomas Williams. Paine helped found Theophilanthropy in Paris, promoting reason, science, morality, and humanitarianism, and proposed agrarian justice and neutral maritime cooperation. He remained in Paris, staying with Nicolas de Bonneville’s family, briefly traveled to Belgium to visit Vanhuile in Bruges, and later returned to Paris. After Jefferson invited him to America, Paine planned to leave Europe. In a small Paris room filled with manuscripts and invention models, Henry Redhead Yorke visited him; Paine, initially forgetting Yorke, eventually recognized him emotionally.
